description: Per-family rung-4 (bounded transformer residency) applicability, derived from the pinned inference revision's provider/architecture code. Read by scripts/generate-memory-matrix.mjs, which turns each (family, backend) verdict into the matrix's bounded_transformer_residency cells. Keys are the family group ids from generate-memory-matrix.mjs#familyGroup, which are the family's MLX story id.

structuralApplicability.full: The windowable transformer trunk is ONE uniform stack of interchangeable blocks; a single BlockPlan bounds essentially all of its weight bytes. Only embedders and heads sit outside it.
structuralApplicability.partial: The trunk is not one uniform stack. Any of: it decomposes into two or more separately-indexed stacks (needing a plan each); its single stack mixes block KINDS, so the residency floor is the largest kind rather than an average block; or part of it — a conv trunk, a second resident network — cannot be windowed at all. `blockStacks` names every stack and marks which are windowable. Neither Implemented nor Structurally N/A — recorded as partial rather than rounded to either (SC-15969).
structuralApplicability.none: No uniform sequential block stack exists, so the rung has nothing to bound. Requires `structural` evidence; the matrix cell becomes Structurally N/A.
structuralApplicability.requires-different-primitive: A uniform stack exists, but gen_core::block_window's SHAPE (one carried state, a fresh view per window, release after materialize) cannot express this family's forward. Recorded as a finding rather than as an N/A, per the story: a family that needs a different PRIMITIVE is not a family the rung cannot help. Such a family may never be marked implemented.

implementation.provider-local: Real block streaming that does NOT go through the shared primitive.
implementation.none: No block-window code path exists for this family on this backend.

vocabulary.implementedEntries: Legacy Cartesian implementation selector: the exact catalog entries whose provider exposes one parameter-identical rung-4 code path. Implementation is per ENTRY, not per family — Krea's Candle contract is gated on the turbo descriptor id, so krea_2_raw does not get it — and a family-level claim would over-report. Mutually exclusive with `implementationScopes`; must be empty exactly when `implementation` is "none".
vocabulary.implementationScopes: Exact implementation selectors for a family whose entries or tiers publish different rung-4 parameter shapes. Every scope names entries and its own strategyParameters; optional tiers, modes, and overlays narrow the scope. Scopes must not overlap and are mutually exclusive with the legacy implementedEntries/implementedTiers/implementedModes/implementedOverlays fields.
vocabulary.implementedModes: Optional narrowing of `implementedEntries` to the catalog modes the implementing provider descriptor actually serves. Needed because the matrix collapses a catalog entry's modes onto one provider id while inference may route them to DIFFERENT descriptors: Candle Krea's edit modes are served by the krea_2_edit descriptor and the krea_2_turbo_edit surface tag, neither of which returns the memory contract, so a mode-blind claim would report rung 4 as implemented on a route that does not expose it. Absent means every mode.
vocabulary.implementedTiers: Optional narrowing of legacy `implementedEntries` to measured numeric tiers. Absent means every tier.
vocabulary.implementedOverlays: Optional narrowing of `implementedEntries` to the overlay cells admitted by the provider contract. Absent means every overlay. Use this for evidence-gated exclusions such as a contract measured only with no adapter; use `overlayIncompatible` instead when the provider mechanism makes an overlay structurally impossible.
vocabulary.strategyParameters: The rung's OWN published parameters for a legacy Cartesian implementation claim. Exact implementationScopes carry this field per scope. Deliberately not the cumulative composition: rung 4 engages lower rungs by cost-order default, but inventing unmeasured values would put unsupported numbers in a cell that reads as evidence.
vocabulary.overlayIncompatible: Present when the provider's adapter mechanism makes a windowed block unable to carry an overlay. It makes the overlay cells of the IMPLEMENTED entries/modes Structurally N/A with the cited evidence, and nothing else: on an entry that has no streaming path at all the rung is Missing for the ordinary reason, and calling it structurally exempt would presuppose a path that does not exist. It is reported on the cell as its own `overlayIncompatible` flag rather than by overwriting `structuralApplicability`, whose meaning is about the ARCHITECTURE — Krea's 28-block trunk is windowable whatever its adapters do.
vocabulary.blockStacks[].entries: Optional. Present when a stack exists on only some of the family's catalog entries, so a per-entry difference stays machine-readable instead of being rounded into the family verdict.

requestPeak.moves: Measured to move the REQUEST peak, not merely a phase peak.
requestPeak.does-not-move: Measured, and the request peak did not move. Per the epic's non-negotiable this is not a saving and must not be selected by default.
requestPeak.unmeasured: No request-peak measurement exists for this family/backend at the pinned revision.

vocabulary.requestPeak.byTier: Optional per-tier override of the family/backend request-peak finding. Required when measurements differ by numeric tier; omitted tiers inherit requestPeak.finding.
vocabulary.requestPeak.scopes: Optional exact cell selectors for measurements narrower than a whole family/backend or tier. Each selector may name entries, tiers, modes, and overlays; omitted dimensions are wildcards. A matching selector overrides byTier and finding.
vocabulary.outOfMatrixFamilies: Surveyed families the matrix CANNOT carry a verdict for, keyed by the family's epic id rather than by a familyGroup id it does not have. `families` is fenced to the image catalog in both directions — the generator builds from `manifest.models.filter(type === "image")`, and assertRung4SurveyCoversEveryFamily rejects a survey key the catalog does not advertise — so a video family placed under `families` fails generation outright rather than producing a row. These records are validated by parseOutOfMatrixRung4Families on every generation and are deliberately NOT published into the matrix: they are the survey's own upkeep, so the work is recorded where the next reader looks instead of nowhere. A record whose catalog entries the matrix has since learned is a hard error, which is what moves it into `families` on the day the ladder gains the lane.
vocabulary.outOfMatrixFamilies[].backends[].stacks: Per-stack rung-4 applicability, one entry per separately-indexed stack, each with its own `structuralApplicability` and `reason`. Wider than `families[].blockStacks`, which is denoise-phase only by design: these families are surveyed before any lane exists, and the stack that sets the floor may sit in another phase entirely (MiniMax-H3's does). The family verdict is DERIVED from this list by `deriveOutOfMatrixApplicability` and rejected if it disagrees — one windowable stack and no unwindowable remainder is `full`, no windowable stack at all is `none`, and everything else is `partial`, so the family answer cannot be asserted independently of its stacks. That rule reproduces 38 of the 40 verdicts `families` already carries, not all 40: Qwen-Image (`families.15511`) records `full` on BOTH backends while holding two `blockStacks`, because the second is control-route-only (`entries: ["qwen_image_control"]`) and is not resident on the routes its verdict covers, and the derivation has no notion of route scoping. Route scoping is deliberately not modelled, because no out-of-matrix record needs it to land on the right answer — MiniMax-H3's own route-conditional stack (`text_encoder.vision_tower`, the `fl2va` keyframe path only) is `partial` under either rule. Treat the derivation as the survey's vocabulary for stacks that are unconditionally resident, with route conditionality recorded in a stack's `blocks` or `reason` prose and not yet in the arithmetic.
vocabulary.outOfMatrixFamilies[].backends[].contrac: The inference revision this backend record's `inference:` evidence paths and quoted constants resolve at, as an abbreviated git sha. Required, and it exists because these records are the one part of the survey the matrix's own `generatedFrom.inferenceRevision` does not date: a `families` verdict is surveyed against crates the Cargo pin already carries, while an out-of-matrix record is surveyed BEFORE the lane exists and may cite crates the pinned tree does not contain. MiniMax-H3's do — at the pinned 0e4adc6f neither `mlx-gen-minimax-h3` nor `candle-gen-minimax-h3` is present.
vocabulary.outOfMatrixFamilies[].backends[].state: The published matrix cell's CODE claim, restated on the record in the cell's own five-value vocabulary (sc-17153). Required, and required to AGREE with `contractSupport` under the shared isImplemented() predicate — consumers classify it through that predicate, never by string comparison, so the first promoted (`Verified`) record cannot silently drop out of a coverage count the way SC-16060 describes.
vocabulary.outOfMatrixFamilies[].backends[].memoryC: The published matrix cell's PEAKS claim, kept distinct from `state` (sc-17153). `status` and `coveredPixelBound` are DERIVED from `measuredGeometries` by the shared memoryCharacterization() helper on every generation — asserting them independently is rejected, exactly as the family verdict may not disagree with its stacks — and a characterization other than `unmeasured` on a non-implemented `state` is refused, mirroring the published cell rule. `measuredGeometries` means SceneWorks-side calibration receipts; a `reason` prose field is required so the record says what is measured and what the terminal campaign still owes.
vocabulary.unroutedBackends: Family-level declarations for a backend the routing catalog does not serve. Each declaration carries a reason, owning story, and evidence. It is distinct from a routed backend whose rungs are Missing, and generation fails if the route appears while the declaration remains.
vocabulary.modalityRelationship: Optional explicit relationship between image and video entries that share one surveyed family. Entries remain modality-distinct while provider/architecture facts may be shared; generation validates every named entry against the admitted catalog.

notes: Rung 4's SOLE shared prerequisite is `LoadShape::DeferredMaterialization`. `BOUNDED_TRANSFORMER_RESIDENCY_REQUIRES` names that edge and nothing else — inference `crates/contracts/gen-core/src/memory_strategy.rs:290-293`, the `LoadShape::DeferredMaterialization` identifier itself on line 292, at pinned rev 0e4adc6f. SC-15998 measured the four combinations independently on MLX/Metal and REMOVED the rung-1 edge this note used to assert, because it had encoded one provider's coupled loader shape as universal arithmetic. Three separate facts now have to be kept apart, and this note is where they are stated once. (1) The SHARED graph has no rung edge at all. (2) A PROVIDER may append its own through `MemoryProviderContract::additional_prerequisites`, and several do: mlx-gen-anima and mlx-gen-chroma push `BoundedTransformerResidency -> StagedResidency (EngagedInSameRequest)` when the load is `streamable`, while mlx-gen-bernini deliberately pushes none. So a family entry below saying its window needs rung 1 in the same request can be perfectly true — it is a claim about that provider, checked against that provider, and it belongs in that entry rather than up here. (3) The GENERATOR consumes (2) rather than approximating it. `strategyStatus`'s rung-4 arm walks the same graph `MemoryProviderContract::validate_selection` walks — the shared edge above, then that provider's own appended edges — taking the per-(family, backend) edge set from `config/rung4-contract-prerequisites.json`, which `scripts/rung4-contract-prerequisites.mjs` derives from the pinned revision and `check.yml` re-derives against a shallow fetch of it. Before sc-19542 the arm applied `stagedResidencyIsAvailable` to every family whether or not its provider declared the edge; sc-18664 measured that blanket proxy inert on the catalog as it stood — removing both RUNG-4 call sites, which are the two the rung-4 arm makes and NOT the rung-1 arm's own use of the same predicate, regenerated a byte-identical docs/generated/memory-matrix.json (957,908 B) and .md (16,560 B) — and sc-19542 replaced it with the records. The replacement is inert on today's catalog too, by the same measurement: every cell is byte-identical, and the only generated change is the source-tree revision moving because the records joined SOURCE_PATHS. 21 of the 40 (family, backend) pairs append the rung-1 edge at pinned rev 0e4adc6f and 19 do not, so the predicate now reaches only the 21.

Structural applicability is about the DENOISE trunk. The component-scope axis (Dit / TextEncoder / Both) is a published rung-4 parameter, not a separate rung; where a family's text encoder changes the answer it is recorded in `findings`.

Overlay compatibility is a property of the provider's ADAPTER MECHANISM, not of the architecture: a provider that installs adapters as forward-time residuals can replay them onto a materialized block, while one that folds a delta into the base weight at load cannot. Only the two families with code evidence either way carry an `overlays` finding.

Why `unmeasured` is the honest answer almost everywhere, and why a static proxy will not do. docs/sc-16195/resolution-sweep.json measures, at 1024x1024 on the RESIDENT hold-all path, weight residency against activation transient: illustrious q8 4.74 vs 14.04 GiB, sdxl bf16 6.48 vs 14.04, z-image-turbo q4 5.38 vs 14.04, lens q4 16.46 vs 14.04, qwen-image q8 33.45 vs 7.66, krea-2-turbo q8 18.06 vs 7.67. Weight residency is a MINORITY of that peak on three of the six tiers, which is enough to show rung 4 cannot be assumed to move the request peak — but not enough to predict that it will not, because rung 4 is only ever selected in composition with rungs 2 and 3, which attack exactly the transient term those rows are dominated by. Z-Image is the worked case: its resident-path row looks transient-bound, and once the ladder is engaged its request peak is decode-bound at ~4.36 GiB and rung 4 still moved it. So this axis is decided by a per-family measurement of the rung-3 composition against the rung-4 composition, which is what Krea's Candle evidence records and what no other family has.

What `blockStacks` covers, stated once. It inventories the stacks resident during the DENOISE phase — the trunk a rung-4 window would bound, plus any second network held alongside it (a control branch, an identity path, a second expert), because those set the share of resident transformer weight the rung can actually move. It does NOT inventory text-encoder or vision-tower stacks: those belong to the conditioning phase, they are what rung 1 sheds, and the component-scope parameter (Dit / TextEncoder / Both) is the axis that addresses them. Where a family's encoder changes the rung-4 answer it is recorded in `findings` instead.

An unrouted backend is a routing fact, not five implementation verdicts. Video families must declare every absent family-level backend under `unroutedBackends`; the generator cross-checks those declarations against the same route oracle that creates matrix lanes and rejects both an undeclared absence and a declaration that outlives a newly added route.

17137.name: MiniMax-H3 (Hailuo 3.0)
17137.whyOutOfMatrix: The memory matrix is image-only by construction: scripts/generate-memory-matrix.mjs builds from `manifest.models.filter((model) => model.type === "image")`, and `minimax_h3` / `minimax_h3_ref` are `"type": "video"`. Putting this family under `families` is not merely inert, it fails generation — assertRung4SurveyCoversEveryFamily runs the survey -> catalog direction too and throws `family SC-… carries a mlx verdict, but the catalog advertises no mlx entry in that family — the verdict reaches no cell (SC-15969)`, which was reproduced against this exact record before it was placed here. There is also no `familyGroup` id to key it by, because `familyGroup` throws on `minimax_h3`. So the honest shape is a record the generator validates and does not publish, keyed by the epic id, rather than a family row the ladder cannot express. One consequence has to be stated rather than left to be inferred: this record is NOT dated by the matrix's own `generatedFrom.inferenceRevision`. Every `inference:` path and every byte constant below resolves at its backend's `contractRevision` — e09f46aafb10126b14172a148acb26c619cf9213 for the MLX record (sc-18662's streamed-request measurement), 79f02e6d0eaca861a0698ee490b70daa7441e321 for the Candle one — each a descendant of the pinned 0e4adc6f at which neither `mlx-gen-minimax-h3` nor `candle-gen-minimax-h3` exists at all. Each backend carries that sha in `contractRevision`, which the generator requires; the corrected `notes[0]` prerequisite claim is separately anchored at 0e4adc6f, where gen-core's contract constant does live.

mlx.stateReason: The matrix-cell vocabulary's CODE claim, kept distinct from `memoryCharacterization` exactly as a published cell keeps them (sc-17153; SC-16060 is where conflating them bit). `Implemented/unverified` because the contract declares rung 4 Implemented at `contractRevision` and the streamed request executed — but no SceneWorks calibration receipt binds it: config/memory-calibration-plan.json has no minimax rows and docs/generated/memory-calibration-evidence.json has no minimax records, and `Runtime verified` / `Verified` are receipt-backed states. Consumers must classify this through the shared isImplemented() predicate (generate-memory-matrix.mjs), never by string-comparing the state — the validator enforces agreement with `contractSupport` through that predicate for exactly that reason.
mlx.contractReason: sc-18662 landed both deferred loaders, so rung 4 is `MemoryStrategySupport::Implemented` on a `LoadShape::DeferredMaterialization` load and `Missing` on a resident one — the contract now honours the spec's shape (`resolved_load_shape`) instead of pinning `EagerMaterialization`, because `MiniMaxH3Dit::load_dir_deferred` and `MiniMaxH3TextEncoder::from_dir_deferred` both exist and are measured. `lifecycle.transformer_window_materialization` tracks the same resolved shape. The published domain is `transformer_window_sizes: [1]` and `transformer_window_components: [Both]`. The singleton is a MEASURED finding, not a default — but as of sc-17153 the finding is that WINDOW 1 IS THE RESIDENCY FLOOR, not that the parameter is inert, and the inertness justification this field used to carry is RETRACTED. Re-measured 2026-08-20 on real weights (Apple/Metal, quiet host) by inference PR #718 (`claude/sc-17153-dense-te-window-zeros`), a DESCENDANT of this record's `contractRevision` that was still open when this was written — so the figures below are the corrections that revision carries, not what e09f46aaf declares. Inertness survives only on the DiT arms, where `run_windowed` releases each block as it is consumed rather than at the window boundary, so even a 50-block all-covering plan holds one block at a time: 1.12x (q4) and 1.13x (q8) spread across [1,5,10,50], against 8.85x / 13.73x / 20.82x below resident at q4 / q8 / bf16 (`RUNG4_DIT_MEASURED_PEAKS`). It does NOT survive on the text encoder — and because the published component scope is `Both`, the window covers the encoder too, so the DiT result cannot carry the domain by itself. Across the same [1,5,10,50] the encoder spreads 1.39x on dense bf16 (53.07 GB resident; 4.50 / 6.24 / 6.24 / 6.24 GB), 2.17x on q8 (26.98 GB resident; 1.43 / 2.65 / 2.78 / 3.10 GB) and 2.45x on q4 (14.43 GB resident; 0.80 / 1.78 / 1.95 / 1.87 GB), with the packed spread observed anywhere from 2.17x to 3.12x across runs — the 3.12x by epic 17137's own terminal measurement campaign. The window parameter is therefore a REAL LEVER on every encoder a tiered render conditions through, and the `< 2.0` spread assertion that used to guard this in `inference:crates/media/mlx-gen/mlx-gen-minimax-h3/tests/block_window_real.rs` was asserting something false about them; it has been retired. What the singleton `[1]` domain rests on instead is the one property that holds on every arm with a wide margin: window 1 is the measured MINIMUM, and every larger window measured holds strictly more. So `[1]` is the cheapest point of a real curve rather than an arbitrary one, and publishing the other values would advertise a lever that trades memory away; the arm now asserts that floor and merely REPORTS the spread. The retracted prior text — 1.09x and 1.20x across [1,5,10,50] on two runs, said to independently reproduce SC-15448's window-inert-above-1 finding on another family — was taken on the DENSE encoder alone, where a single Qwen3 layer's f32 upcast dominates the peak at every window size and flattens the curve (that arm now re-measures 1.39x). SC-15448's window-inert-above-1 finding is NOT reproduced on this family and must not be cited from this row. `Both` rather than `Dit` because the conditioning stage is still the taller of the two at every tier even after sc-19120's packed encoder, and it is the larger absolute saving (47.26 GB against the DiT's 37.68 GB at bf16). One family-specific hazard is recorded in `inference:crates/media/mlx-gen/mlx-gen-minimax-h3/src/block_stream.rs`: `adaln_proj` is 39.3% of the DiT and sc-17145's precompute already consumes it once per request, so a denoise window must materialize block BODIES only — a window that re-read it would cost 26.02 GB per step and produce bit-identical output, which no equivalence test could catch. The once-per-request projection pass is windowed separately (`precompute_adaln_windowed`), because it is the larger of the two residencies and every prior adopter windows only the per-step walk.

requestPeak.reason: Measured on the shipped `generate` (sc-18662): one end-to-end t2va render through the deferred loaders — q4 DiT tier, q4 packed text encoder, 124 frames at 384x224, 4 steps, window 1, `TransformerComponent::Both` — peaked at 5.80 GB (5,804,369,044 B, `RUNG4_REQUEST_PEAK_Q4_BYTES`), attributed per stage: conditioning 0.78, dit-load + adaln-precompute 2.03, denoise 2.03, decode 5.80. The request is DECODE-bound, which is exactly what the phase envelope's max(TE, DiT, decode) arithmetic predicted (5.77 GB) before any request ran — against the resident request's 53.07 GB conditioning mark, a 9.1x whole-request reduction. What changed since the last survey of this row: `MiniMaxH3::requested_transformer_window` now admits the streamed selection and routes ALL THREE conditioning paths (t2va / fl2va / ref2va) through `from_dir_deferred` + `set_block_window` and the denoise through `load_dir_deferred` + `JointDit::new_windowed`, so the rung is reachable from a request rather than only from its own harness. The harness holds the figure to a ±25% declared-vs-measured band, and both real-weight guards were mutation-checked on device — a stale declared constant and a silent resident downgrade each red the test. Scope stated rather than implied: the measured request cell is q4/q4 at 124 frames; q8 and bf16 request compositions are unmeasured cells (the per-arm cells bound them — conditioning 53.07 -> 4.50 GB and denoise 39.58 -> 1.90 / 21.64 -> 1.58 / 12.00 -> 1.36 GB across bf16/q8/q4 — but a bound is not a measurement), and the decode stage this request pins at is tier-independent. TWO CORRECTIONS to that parenthesis, both from sc-17153, re-measured 2026-08-20 on real weights (Apple/Metal, quiet host) and landing in inference PR #718 (`claude/sc-17153-dense-te-window-zeros`) — a descendant of this record's `contractRevision` that was still open when this was written, so neither correction is what e09f46aaf declares. (1) THE WINDOWED CONDITIONING FIGURE WAS A STALE CONSTANT, not a new result. `RUNG4_TE_WINDOWED_PEAK_BYTES` reads 5_814_845_376 B (5.81 GB) at `contractRevision` and does not reproduce: eight runs land at 4_501_440_448 B (4.50 GB) ± ~0.5 MB, 1.31 GB / 22.6% below the declared value, and window 1 measured that same figure IDENTICALLY before and after sc-17153's `from_dir_deferred` token-table fix — so it is drift from sc-18662, NOT an artifact of a degenerate run. Its partner `RUNG4_TE_RESIDENT_PEAK_BYTES` is CONFIRMED: 53,072,280,000 B measured against 53,074,721,216 B declared, Δ 2.4 MB. That is precisely the single-member drift a ±25% QUOTIENT band cancels and a per-constant ABSOLUTE bound catches, which is why sc-17153 replaced the ratio band. The corrected pair is 53.07 -> 4.50 GB, an 11.79x reduction where the stale pair implied 9.13x. (2) "BIT-IDENTICAL OUTPUT THROUGHOUT" IS RETRACTED FOR THE DENSE (bf16) ENCODER AND RETAINED EVERYWHERE ELSE. It holds — asserted as relative max-abs exactly 0.0 at every window — on all three DiT tiers, and on the PACKED q4/q8 encoders that every tiered render actually conditions through, which sc-17153's `the_packed_text_encoder_arm_is_measured_per_window` covers for the first time (before it, the packed windowed output was compared against nothing). It does not hold unconditionally on the dense encoder, which has been observed returning an ALL-ZERO conditioning context: identical shapes, clean exit, no Metal diagnostic, max 0.0 where the correct answer is 1.55e4. Its characterization is stated here so this row is not misread as a rung-4 or windowing defect, because it is neither. Four sightings in ~30 real-weight forwards on this hardware (~13%), EVERY one on the bf16 dense encoder and zero across ~12 packed q4/q8 arms. It is NOT windowing: two of the four were plain RESIDENT forwards, one of them after the loader fix, on a path that never reaches `from_dir_deferred`. It is NOT the window size: reversing [1,5,10,50] to [50,10,5,1] moved the zero from window 1 to window 50, so it follows whichever forward runs first after a 53 GB load rather than the parameter. It correlates with a slow, cold read of the 62 GB component, but did not reproduce in 16 warm runs nor in a deliberately cold run with the page cache evicted to 60 MB of free pages. THE MECHANISM IS BELOW THE mlx-gen CRATE AND IS UNATTRIBUTED; nothing here claims it has been removed, and rung 4 neither causes it nor is more exposed to it than the resident path — so it must not be recorded against this row's `requestPeak` finding, against the singleton window domain, or as a rung-4 defect anywhere else. What exists today is DETECTION, not a fix: both TE arms now compare the context against a reference and refuse a degenerate one, which caught the fourth sighting live, and a runtime degeneracy refusal is being added separately. The peak counter reads LOWER when the work does not happen, so no memory assertion in this rung can see it, and neither can a norm, a cosine or a checksum. The streamed request measured above is unaffected in either direction: it conditioned through the q4 PACKED encoder, on which there is no sighting. Streaming is refused with adapters configured (a window rebuilds blocks from the staged tier, so a folded LoRA would be silently dropped), on a resident load shape, on any component scope but `Both`, and on any window but 1. The earlier epic framing — that H3's peak is flat because it is activation-dominated, or set by denoise, so the quant tiers buy disk but not memory — remains RETRACTED and must not be reproduced from this row.

memoryCharacterization.reason: The matrix-cell vocabulary's PEAKS claim, distinct from `state` (sc-17153). STRUCTURE NOW, NUMBERS AT THE TERMINAL CAMPAIGN — honestly split: `status`/`coveredPixelBound` are DERIVED from `measuredGeometries` by the shared memoryCharacterization() helper on every generation (asserting them independently is rejected, mirroring deriveOutOfMatrixApplicability), and `measuredGeometries` is empty because characterization here means SceneWorks-side calibration receipts, of which zero exist for this family. sc-18662's 384x224 streamed receipt is an inference-side TEST receipt at this record's `contractRevision` — a revision the app does not pin — and per-(tier x duration) cells are required anyway because `frames` is an exact-match evidence key (mlx_fit_gate.rs) and fitted-curve extrapolation scales by area only, so one point could not stand in for the duration axis even if it were admissible. stacks.blocks: 50 uniform `Qwen3DecoderLayer` — `SELECT_HIDDEN` = 50 of the checkpoint's 64, and layers 50-63 are never loaded or run

This is also the stack that matters most here: it is the 53.07 GB conditioning mark, and rung 4's `TransformerComponent` scope axis (Dit / TextEncoder / Both) already exists to address exactly it. `componentBytes` is the whole `text_encoder/` component (66,714,912,872 B, `TEXT_ENCODER_BYTES`), not this stack's share, which no source splits out.

stacks.blocks: Qwen3-VL vision tower — 351 `model.visual.*` tensors, `fl2va` keyframe path only
stacks.reason: Reuses `mlx_gen_boogu::vision::VisionTower`, which holds `blocks: Vec<Block>` with `patch_embed` / `pos_embed` / mergers outside it. Uniform in its own right, but separately indexed from the language tower and only present when a keyframe is conditioned — so it needs its own plan, which is one of the two reasons the family answer is `partial` rather than `full`.

`MiniMaxH3Dit` holds `blocks: Vec<DitBlock>` built over `0..cfg.num_layers` from one constructor, with `context_embedder`, `norm_out` and the two output heads outside it.
